bullets.body: Unsloth shipped a Tuesday point release tagged v2026.5.26 introducing first-class support for Alibaba's Qwen3.6-Max-Preview as a fine-tuning base, with the Daniel Han Chen and Mike Han Chen author pair posting a paired benchmark sheet on the Hugging Face Blog showing that the new Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B Mixture-of-Experts checkpoint trains at roughly 1.74x throughput against the prior DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe under the same router-only LoRA driver on a single 8x H200 SXM5 node, with a measured peak combined VRAM reduction of 11.3 percent versus a vanilla Hugging Face Transformers v5 baseline and an additional 4.1 percent peak savings against last week's Mixtral-Next 70B merge. The release also lifts the contributed 60B-class recipe count to four — adding a community-tested MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE port from a Tsinghua University KEG Lab pull request on top of the existing DeepSeek R3-Pro, OLMo-2 60B and Qwen3 MoE 60B set — and introduces a new selective-expert-checkpoint primitive that lets the trainer freeze inactive expert columns on disk during checkpoint write, cutting checkpoint disk footprint on the MiniMax port from roughly 470GB to 188GB across the first ten saved revisions. A Tuesday Simon Willison note flagged the selective-expert-checkpoint primitive as the most operationally meaningful change Unsloth has shipped this quarter for consumer-class downstream fine-tuners running on Lambda Labs or RunPod with attached SSD budget caps, and a separate Tuesday Hacker News thread surfaced two early independent reproductions of the Qwen3.6-Max-Preview benchmark on 8x H200 SXM5 rentals from CoreWeave and Crusoe Cloud with throughput numbers landing inside 3 percent of the Daniel Han Chen sheet.

bullets.body: Alibaba's Qwen team published the formal Qwen3.6-Max-Preview model card on Hugging Face on Tuesday morning Pacific time, lifting the architecture from a preview-numbers-only blog post to a fully gated open-weight release under the Tongyi Qianwen open license, with the 235B-active-parameter Mixture-of-Experts checkpoint shipping a 1M-token native context window, a 24-of-160 expert routing topology, and a published instruction-tuned variant alongside the base. Per the model card, Qwen3.6-Max-Preview lands at 88.7 on LiveCodeBench v6 and 76.2 on SWE-Bench Verified — both new records for any non-Anthropic non-OpenAI checkpoint — and matches Claude Opus 4.7 on AIME 2025 inside a 0.6-point band. Decrypt confirmed that the release is timed to undercut DeepSeek-V4-Pro's pricing curve heading into the May 28 OpenRouter integration cycle, with Alibaba Cloud Model Studio listing the hosted variant at $0.45 per million input tokens against DeepSeek-V4-Pro's $1.10 floor and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 at $7.50, while The Decoder reported initial Together AI and Fireworks AI hosted endpoints lighting up inside the first six hours with first-token-latency at roughly 0.18 seconds on 8x H100 SXM5 with full FP8 quantization.

bullets.body: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) reopened after the Memorial Day market closure with a Tuesday session that printed the highest single-day volume the stock has carried since the post-Alphabet analyst-day Friday and resolved the three-day pent-up demand from the holiday hold into a clean tape session. The open print landed at $213.40 against Friday's $209.85 close (roughly +1.7 percent gap), reached an intraday high of $221.20 inside the first ninety minutes, and closed at $217.05 on volume of approximately 18.6 million shares — about 2.7x the trailing-twenty-day average and the fifth-highest volume session of the post-IPO record. Bloomberg flagged the close as the first push of the consensus analyst spread above $215, with Bernstein lifting its Market-Perform floor to $200 from $185 in a Tuesday morning note and UBS upgrading Cerebras to Buy with a $240 target citing the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU formally closing Tuesday afternoon at a disclosed $1.2 billion total contract value over four years for first-generation CS-4 capacity placement in the King Abdullah Economic City data-center park. Reuters separately reported institutional buyside cumulative net position lifting to approximately 47.5 percent of float on Tuesday tape from Friday's roughly 44 percent, and Morgan Stanley's Tuesday tape-recap pushed its upside-scenario probability to 61 percent from Friday's 54 percent.

bullets.body: Stellantis disclosed Tuesday morning that its Detroit Mack Avenue Optimus pilot has been advanced from the originally announced June 8 activation date to June 1, with Reuters citing a Stellantis Tuesday note confirming that the 60-unit cohort has completed factory-acceptance testing at Tesla's Fremont commissioning floor inside Memorial Day weekend and that the units have already been wheeled onto the Detroit floor for final fixture mating ahead of the production line restart. The pull-in compresses the gap between the Tesla Fremont 240-unit completion and the first US contract-manufacturing deployment to a single week, and BMW responded inside the same trading session with a press release stating that BMW Plant Leipzig will lock its second AEON cohort first-activation date at June 15 rather than the prior June 22 placeholder, putting four humanoid-robot factory-floor activations inside an 18-day window between June 1 and June 18. Volkswagen Wolfsburg held its June 22 cohort activation but added a 24-unit second cohort with a July 13 target, and Bloomberg reported that Boston Dynamics Hyundai held an investor briefing Tuesday afternoon flagging that the Atlas commercial-fleet first-deployment cycle (Hyundai Motor Group Pyeongtaek plant) is being moved up by roughly nine days to June 24, citing the Stellantis pull-in as the public proof that humanoid factory deployments have crossed the practical readiness threshold.

bullets.body: GitHub Security Lab published a Tuesday advisory disclosing CVE-2026-46127, a critical-severity (CVSS 9.4) prompt-injection-escalation vulnerability in OpenAI's open-source Codex CLI v3.1.x development branch in which an attacker can chain a workspace-scoped sandboxed Codex agent into an unsandboxed shell-exec context via a crafted MCP-server response that exploits a missing JSON-Schema validation step in the agent harness's tool-call deserialization path. The advisory credits researchers Trail of Bits Vasilios Mavroudis and Pillar Security Dor Sarig for the report and notes that OpenAI shipped a patched v3.1.10 development tag inside the disclosure window, with the patched build adding strict schema validation plus a runtime tool-call audit log; the disclosure lifts the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy to twelve catalogued instances, the first net-new addition since the May 8 cycle. The Hacker News reported that CISA placed CVE-2026-46127 on its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog inside the same Tuesday window after a Mandiant incident-response engagement at a Fortune 500 financial-services customer confirmed active exploitation in the wild, and OpenAI's Tuesday security note stated that the Codex CLI's production-tier auto-update path will force-roll all v3.1.x development tenants to v3.1.10 inside a 72-hour window. Separately, NIST NVD published a Tuesday afternoon update confirming the CVSS 9.4 scoring and reclassifying the vulnerability under the agent-loader subcategory.
